Who bills what in Phoenix

  • Maricopa County Assessor's Office handles assessment.
  • Maricopa County Treasurer bills and collects the tax.

Due dates

First half due Oct 1, delinquent after 5:00 p.m. Nov 1 (bills over $100); second half due Mar 1, delinquent after 5:00 p.m. May 1; full-year payment delinquent after 5:00 p.m. Dec 31. Text from the Treasurer FAQ search excerpt; the page was fetched but extraction did not return the text. Home page confirms 2026 full-year deadline of Dec 31.. See the official page.

Challenging your assessment

Petition for Review of Real Property Valuation must be filed with the Assessor within 60 days of the mail date on the Notice of Value; appeals can be filed online (Notice of Claim page opened).. See the official page.

Tax rate

We could not confirm the current Phoenix rate on an opened page, so we do not state one.

Local notes

  • Arizona: the County Assessor sets full cash/limited property values; the County Treasurer bills and collects all property taxes (including city levies). Cities do not assess or collect.
  • Census Vintage 2025 population 1665481; county Maricopa County from Census SUMLEV 157.

Phoenix by the numbers

The Census Bureau's 2019-2023 survey counts about 1,624,832 people in Phoenix, which makes it the 1st largest of the 38 az places we cover. The median value of an owner-occupied home is $381,900, 7% above the median of those 38 places. 57% of occupied homes are owner-occupied and 43% are rented, against a median of 72% owner-occupancy across the az places. The median home was built in 1984, about 39 years ago, which matters for roofs, plumbing and inspection requests. These numbers describe Phoenix as a whole, so a given street can sit well above or below them.
